correctness.rationale: For theta in [0,1], Fθ′=fθ and Fθ″=1−θ+θ sech²(z/2)>0 yield proper strictly convex Hamiltonian ovals and unit small-amplitude frequency. On each level radial r(E,phi) strictly increases with E, and angular rate Omega=(1−theta)+theta*sum_(u=cos,sin)u² Q(ru), Q(z)=2tanh(z/2)/z strictly decreasing for positive |z|. Thus T0=2π; Tθ(E) strictly increases for theta>0, with Taylor small-E 2π(1+theta E/8+O(E²)). For fixed theta<1, dominated convergence gives plateau 2π/(1−theta); at theta=1 the large-E diamond yields T/E→1. Under epsilon=1−theta, V=epsilon*v,W=epsilon*w,s=epsilon*t, energy e=epsilon E, limit G0(z)=z²/2+2|z| and linear translated circular quadrant arcs yield epsilon*T(e/epsilon)→8 atan sqrt(1+e/2)−2π. Direct independent angular geometry identity checked at e=.4,1,3,8; inspected verify_period.py uses finite numeric corroboration, not proof of universal limit.
